draft.title: Polarity of bonds and molecules
card: Electronegativity is how strongly an atom pulls shared electrons towards itself. When two bonded atoms differ in electronegativity, the shared pair sits closer to one atom.
Polar bond
a bond between atoms with different electronegativities. The atom with the stronger pull gains a slight negative charge and the other a slight positive charge.
Non-polar bond
a bond between atoms with the same, or almost the same, electronegativity, so the electrons are shared evenly.
Polar molecule
a molecule whose shape leaves the charges uneven, so one side is slightly negative and the other slightly positive. If polar bonds are arranged so their pulls cancel, the molecule is non-polar.
draft.remember: Unequal pull makes a bond polar. Uneven charge across the whole shape makes a molecule polar.

a.q: Why is the bond in a hydrogen chloride molecule, H-Cl, polar?
opts: Chlorine pulls the shared pair harder than hydrogen does
Hydrogen and chlorine share their electrons equally
Chlorine gives one of its electrons fully to hydrogen
Hydrogen pulls the shared pair harder than chlorine does
a.why: Chlorine and hydrogen differ in electronegativity, so the shared pair sits closer to chlorine, which becomes slightly negative. Equal sharing would make the bond non-polar.
a.clue: Think about which atom pulls the shared pair harder.

b.q: A molecule has two polar bonds pointing in exactly opposite directions from the central atom, so the pulls cancel. How is the molecule best described?
opts: Non-polar, because the charges are spread evenly
Polar, because each bond is polar
Non-polar, because its bonds are non-polar
Polar, because the central atom is slightly positive
b.why: Opposite pulls cancel, so the charges are even across the molecule and it is non-polar, even though each bond is polar. Having polar bonds does not make a molecule polar when the shape evens out the charges.
b.clue: Look at what the two equal pulls do to each other.

a.best: Chlorine pulls the shared pair harder than hydrogen does

b.best: Non-polar, because the charges are spread evenly

proposal.title: Polarity of bonds and molecules
card: Electronegativity is how strongly an atom pulls shared electrons towards itself. It rises across a period and up a group, so fluorine is the highest, and chlorine is higher than hydrogen.
Polar bond
a bond between atoms with different electronegativities. The shared pair sits closer to the atom with the stronger pull, which gains a slight negative charge, and the other a slight positive charge.
Non-polar bond
a bond between atoms with the same, or almost the same, electronegativity, so the electrons are shared evenly.
Polar molecule
a molecule whose shape leaves the charges uneven, so one side is slightly negative and the other slightly positive. If polar bonds are arranged so their pulls cancel, the molecule is non-polar.
proposal.remember: Unequal pull makes a bond polar. Uneven charge across the whole shape makes a molecule polar.
